title: Minimum obstacles to remove
statement: A grid has 0 (empty) and 1 (obstacle) cells. Moving into an obstacle costs 1 (you remove it); moving into an empty cell costs 0. Return the minimum number of obstacles to remove to get from the top-left to the bottom-right cell (4-directional).
hints: Shortest path where every edge costs 0 or 1.
A deque: push 0-cost moves to the front, 1-cost moves to the back.

solution.explanation: 0-1 BFS: the deque stays sorted by distance (front ≤ back ≤ front + 1), so it behaves like Dijkstra's heap without the log factor. Recognising "weights are only 0 and 1" saves the heap; with a 250 × 250 grid, that matters in Python.
